items.title: A benchmarking framework for organoid computing
items.why: Proposes qualification criteria for organoids, interfaces and stimulation-evoked computation, aiming at reproducible comparison across labs. Abstract read; a framework, not a performance result.

items.title: A Mark of the Noncognitive
items.why: Philosophy paper proposing a principled criterion for what is clearly not cognitive, as a way through the basal-cognition definition dispute. Abstract read.

items.title: A minimal model of cognition based on oscillatory and current-based reinforcement processes
items.why: A mathematical model of how oscillation plus reinforcement could coordinate resources in organisms without nervous systems. Abstract read.

items.title: bioelectrics
items.why: MIT-licensed differentiable PyTorch simulator of membrane voltage in non-neural tissue; runs on a laptop CPU, per its page. Not run by the lab.

items.title: Classification using hyperdimensional computing: a review with comparative analysis
items.why: A reproducible comparison of hyperdimensional classifiers on seven benchmarks and 121 tabular tasks.

items.title: Coding agents as compilers through computational worlds
items.why: A post on coding agents as optimizing compilers, with progressive lowering of software intent through verified computational worlds.

items.title: Encoding tactile stimuli for Braille recognition with organoids
items.why: Bristol study: three FinalSpark organoids classify 26 Braille letters at 83%; the stimulus pattern alone scores 82%. The tissue's edge is robustness to corrupted channels.

items.title: Encoding Tactile Stimuli for Braille Recognition with Organoids
items.why: Organoids on electrode arrays classify Braille patterns; the open question is how much the stimulus code and classifier contribute.

items.title: Engineering Basal Cognition: Minimal Genetic Circuits for Habituation, Sensitization, and Massed–Spaced Learning
items.why: Synthetic-biology design of small genetic circuits that reproduce learning-like behaviours seen in single cells and slime moulds. Abstract read.

items.title: Essay Archive · Ranganaut
items.why: An archive of 803 essays written between 2005 and 2026, offered as a set of trails to walk.

items.title: It's My Act of Worlding But It's Your Moribund Problem
items.why: An essay on worlding as an act that negates what it displaces, read through the film Opus and Nietzsche's force.

items.title: NeuroBridge
items.why: MIT-licensed analysis software for electrode-array recordings (spike rasters, bursts, transfer entropy); advertises a public FinalSpark dataset. Unvetted by the lab.

items.title: Organoid intelligence (OI): the new frontier in biocomputing and intelligence-in-a-dish
items.why: The 2023 roadmap that named the field and made the brain-versus-supercomputer efficiency argument; a vision paper, not measured organoid computing.

items.title: Plato's Key
items.why: Reports that a rotation and one scale let one LLM use another's internal representations of facts, a median 41% transfer accuracy across 12 models.

items.title: Rules for Biologically Inspired Adaptive Network Design
items.why: Tero et al. 2010: slime mould networks with efficiency, fault tolerance and cost comparable to the Tokyo rail system; the source of a much-retold story. Abstract read.

items.title: Tech predictions for 2027 and beyond
items.why: Werner Vogels' annual forecast; its 'computing returns to biology' and 'mind becomes readable' sections bet on neuromorphic chips, living neurons and non-invasive brain interfaces.

items.title: The Future Needs Furniture
items.why: Venkatesh Rao sorts realities into hard/oozy and analytic/constitutive regimes and argues for a playability frontier that intelligence cannot cross.

items.title: The NeuroBench framework for benchmarking neuromorphic computing algorithms and systems
items.why: Community benchmark framework built because neuromorphic results lacked standard comparisons with conventional hardware.

items.title: Torchhd
items.why: MIT-licensed PyTorch library for hyperdimensional computing and vector-symbolic architectures.

items.title: Why AI will not speed up science (yet)
items.why: A geneticist argues, with Amdahl's law, that biomedical research is paced by grants, approvals, animals and people, which AI does not yet speed up.

items.title: A thermodynamically favoured molecular computer
items.why: Open-access Nature paper: a DNA scaffold computer whose answer is the most stable arrangement; ten programs at four sites near 95% yield, a 25-site addition taking up to 14 hours. No energy per computation reported.

items.title: Beyond the Edge of Chaos: Stability-Expressivity Transfer in Reservoir Forecasting
items.why: July 2026 study: the best spectral radius for forecasting matches none of three Lyapunov edges of a reservoir; proposes an index that predicts it.

items.title: Energy-efficient time series processing in real-time with fluidic iontronic memristor circuits
items.why: Simulated iontronic reservoir circuit predicting a chaotic series at an estimated 15.8 pW; authors note the comparison excludes peripheral circuitry.

items.title: Implementation of Reservoir Computing Using Coupled Microelectromechanical Drum Resonators via Sideband-Pumped Phonon-Cavity Dynamics
items.why: Measured MHz MEMS reservoir chip: NARMA-10 error 0.6-0.8; 12.5 fJ per input counts only electrical drive, 8.3 pJ mechanical per input.

items.title: Memristive Physical Reservoir Computing
items.why: 2026 review comparing electrically and optically driven memristor reservoirs from device to system level.

items.title: Molecular computation at equilibrium via programmable entropy
items.why: DNA circuits that program the equilibrium state through entropy, with Boolean logic and reversible signals.

items.title: Multistable Physical Neural Networks
items.why: Bistable mechanical networks that link computation to physical action (Israeli group, 2025).

items.title: Mutual Information and the Edge of Chaos in Reservoir Computers
items.why: Simulations of several reservoir computers: tuning to the edge of chaos does not guarantee the best performance; notes the limited parameter range of physical systems.

items.title: OpenPRC
items.why: Apache-2.0 framework for simulating and evaluating mechanical reservoirs (mass-spring, origami).

items.title: Peppercorn enumerator
items.why: Open tool that enumerates reactions of DNA strand-displacement designs and simulates their kinetics.

items.title: PHRESCO 2026
items.why: Examples of a crumpled-paper reservoir driven by an Arduino and tracked by phone camera, with NARMA evaluation.

items.title: Physical neural networks using sharpness-aware training
items.why: Training that tolerates model mismatch and drift: 97% vs 80% on digits for a microring chip when the digital model was wrong.

items.title: Physical reservoir computing for Edge AI applications
items.why: 2025 review of neuromorphic devices as physical reservoirs, with the open problems of latency, energy and multimodal use.

items.title: PyTorch-ONN
items.why: MIT-licensed simulation and training of optical neural networks with non-ideality injection.

items.title: RCbench
items.why: Open Python toolkit for reservoir benchmarks: NARMA, memory capacity, and loaders for physical-reservoir data.

items.title: Scalable physical deep learning using optical dynamics with state-skipping training and single-map architecture
items.why: Optoelectronic physical learning with a training rule that skips states, claiming roughly 40% less computation.

items.title: The Scale-Intelligence Tradeoff
items.why: Essay arguing that a task's intrinsic scale is how rarely it interrupts the human, so the largest agent swarms probably do routine work; cites Brooks's law for agents.

items.title: Training of physical neural networks
items.why: Nature review of methods for training neural networks implemented in optical, electronic and mechanical systems.

items.title: 'Just Ridiculous': A Famed Philosopher Takes on AI Consciousness (WIRED)
items.why: Interview in which a philosopher doubts AI systems are conscious yet allows non-biological conscious beings in principle, and worries about lost human intellectual effort.

items.title: AI as a tool that allows selection pressure to act on code (Aneesh Sathe)
items.why: A reply to the Regenerable Software essay arguing software has an ecological niche, so cheaper regeneration speeds a Red Queen race rather than ending it. An argument, not a measurement.

items.title: Asymmetric Evolution (symmetry, broken)
items.why: Part of a series on a 'synchronization tax': the thermodynamic cost of keeping systems' descriptions in agreement. A theory essay, assuming the series' earlier parts.

items.title: Bayesian inference with a polymer probabilistic computer
items.why: Four conjugated-polymer probabilistic bits sampling 16-state Bayesian posteriors within the spread expected of ideal bits.

items.title: Coherence at 300 Kelvin (symmetry, broken)
items.why: A long theory essay linking Landauer's floor, multiplicative noise and attention dynamics, with a list of falsifiable tests and Pythia experiments; it compares brain and chatbot energy per bit.

items.title: Could a computer scientist build a brain?
items.why: An essay reading evolution, development and learning as one process on different time scales, with the genome as a compressed record that development unfolds.

items.title: Eric Raymond on 'hot-state dependency'
items.why: A short post defining hot-state dependency: a system that depends on relationships and operational knowledge existing only in its running configuration, and 'heat death' when it crashes and cannot be rebuilt.

items.title: Evaluating Positive Feedback Adiabatic Logic in 16nm FinFET with a Realistic Power-Clock
items.why: A simulation study of adiabatic logic at 16 nm finding energy advantages over static CMOS in small circuits, and three sources of loss that limit them.

items.title: Extreme Event Likelihoods with Guided Generative Models
items.why: A vendor blog on guiding a diffusion climate emulator toward tropical cyclones to estimate odds ratios; an example of generative models as risk-analysis tools.

items.title: How much energy does ChatGPT use? (Epoch AI)
items.why: Epoch AI's estimate of about 0.3 Wh for a typical GPT-4o text query, with its assumptions, and why older estimates were ten times higher.

items.title: IBM Quantum Open Plan updates
items.why: Describes free access to real quantum hardware (10 minutes per 28 days) for outsiders.

items.title: Information and thermodynamics: experimental verification of Landauer's Erasure principle
items.why: A colloidal-particle one-bit memory whose mean heat of erasure saturates at the Landauer bound for slow cycles: the principle measured, not just argued.

items.title: Ingressing Minds: Causal, Non-Physical Patterns In-Form Natural, Synthetic, and Hybrid Embodiments
items.why: Michael Levin's theoretical paper proposing that mathematical patterns relate to physical objects as minds relate to bodies; a philosophical proposal, not an experiment.

items.title: Introducing Un-0: Generating Images with Coupled Oscillators
items.why: A start-up's post on a simulated oscillator network that generates images (FID 6.74 on ImageNet 64x64); no hardware energy measured. Weights and code released.

items.title: Magic state cultivation on Willow
items.why: Google's account of a roughly 40-fold error reduction for magic states and 99.99% logical T-state fidelity on its Willow chip, published in Science.

items.title: Making Unconventional Computing Practical
items.why: A practitioner's essay arguing that processing-in-memory, neuromorphic and thermodynamic chips reached customers by keeping one benefit and going digital. One author's view.

items.title: Metabiology and the complexity of natural evolution
items.why: An outreach article on Carsetti's view that natural computation is embodied and cannot be reduced to purely syntactic processing; a position, not a measurement.

items.title: Programmable Probabilistic Computer with 1,000,000 p-bits
items.why: Measured: a million probabilistic bits on 18 FPGAs sustaining 10^12 updates a second, checked against a GPU reference on spin-glass optimisation.

items.title: Regenerable Software: A Vision for Agentic Software Engineering (Venkatesh Rao)
items.why: A draft essay proposing a third regime of software engineering where the durable asset is the intelligence needed to regenerate code (specs, assurance), not the code itself. A vision, not evidence.

items.title: s3: Simple Scaling of Swarms via Cooperative Multi-agent RL
items.why: Project page for training leaderless asynchronous swarms of language models with a shared reward, reporting gains over best-of-N from solo agents and carry-over to larger swarms.

items.title: Sensemaking as the Heart of Expertise (Commoncog)
items.why: Cedric Chin on expertise as the ability to build better frames, with a proposed exercise: react to a case, then compare your reaction with an expert's.

items.title: Shaping and Monitoring Models Through Their Internal Representations (Goodfire)
items.why: Goodfire's account of training models by shaping which internal concepts they rely on (curbing sycophancy, reward hacking, X-ray shortcuts), with a hierarchy for measuring monitorability. Company research; a post summarising a longer pape

items.title: The brain is not mental! coupling neuronal and immune cellular processing in human organisms
items.why: A Frontiers paper arguing that cognition is distributed across all the body's cells, not the brain alone; a theoretical argument.

items.title: The future of human coordination
items.why: Venkatesh Rao on why individual 10x-1000x speedups from AI break team coordination in complex, many-layered technical stacks, and what a better coordination design would need.

items.title: The Tacit Knowledge Series
items.why: A long-running series on knowledge that cannot be captured in words and how expertise is acquired.

items.title: The Unbearable Slowness of Being: Why do we live at 10 bits/s?
items.why: Zheng and Meister's estimate that human behavioural throughput is about 10 bits/s against about 10^9 bits/s gathered by the senses, and why that gap is unexplained.

items.title: THRML
items.why: Open-source JAX library for blocked Gibbs sampling and energy-based models, from Extropic.

items.title: When a Fact Becomes History (symmetry, broken)
items.why: An essay arguing a standard objection to relational quantum mechanics fails because reversing a lab that recorded a fact would mean undoing all its copies in the environment.

items.title: WSPC Book Series in Unconventional Computing
items.why: A publisher's series page listing the handbook of unconventional computing and volumes on reversible cellular automata, actin computation, quantum computer music and arts and philosophy.

items.title: Zero (Moving Castles)
items.why: A write-up of fine-tuning an 8B base model into a fixed character, reporting character breaks in 2.8% of conversations against 45.2% for a system-prompted instruct model, plus activation analysis.
